V1_causal_non_uniqueness.conclusion: Two CCAs satisfying Ax1-Ax5 with non-isomorphic causal structures exist. Therefore the causal order type is NOT uniquely fixed by the axioms. Result: (B) Emerges non-uniquely.

V2_causal_cones_unique.conclusion: Given a fixed partial order (M, <=), the future and past cones of each element are uniquely and deterministically computed from Ax2. No additional axiom is needed. Result: (A) Emerges uniquely.

V3_gibbs_uniqueness.conclusion: Given (rank function, beta), the Gibbs distribution is UNIQUELY determined. However, beta is NOT fixed by Ax1-Ax5 — it is a free parameter. Therefore: Gibbs *form* emerges uniquely; its *parameterisation* does not. Result: (A) with caveat — beta remains undetermined.

V4_no_metric.conclusion: The same abstract CCA (A < B < C) is consistent with infinitely many distinct metric spaces. The metric is not an invariant of the CCA. Any fixed-metric claim requires additional axioms. Result: (C) — metric requires external input.
V4_no_metric.obstruction: CCA-IMP-3: CCA provides only a counting measure (rank), not a metric.

dimensional_argument.inference: No combination of dimensionless integers gives m/s without external scales

V5_no_speed_from_rank.conclusion: The rank function (dimensionless integer counts) cannot produce a unique propagation speed (dimensional, units m/s). Infinitely many (a, dt) pairs give identical rank sequences but different c. Result: CCA-IMP-3 confirmed — c is not derivable from Ax1-Ax5.

V6_continuum_non_unique.conclusion: The same abstract 1D causal chain can limit to different continuum manifolds (compact vs non-compact, different curvature of measure) depending on how inter-event spacings are assigned. The continuum limit is NOT unique given only the abstract CCA structure. Result: (C) — continuum requires external input.

V7_metric_gives_speed.added_axiom: SE1: map phi: O -> R^d with spacing a and time step dt

isotropic_case.note: Unique only if a same in all directions AND single time step

anisotropic_case.note: Three different speeds — SE1 alone does not enforce isotropy

V7_metric_gives_speed.conclusion: SE1 (metric embedding) is SUFFICIENT to define propagation speed. But it is not SUFFICIENT to make speed unique unless ALSO: (a) isotropic embedding (equal a in all directions), AND (b) single time step per causal morphism. SE1 alone requires isotropy as a FURTHER additional assumption.

V8_master_equation.conclusion: Given a specific CCA, the discrete master equation is uniquely determined by its weight function ε. BUT different CCAs give different master equations with different stationary distributions. The form (p(t+1) = T p(t)) is uniquely determined from a given CCA; the equation itself is non-unique across the class of all CCAs. Result: (B) emerges non-uniquely.

V9_finite_automorphisms.proof_sketch: |Aut(A)| <= |Sym(Hom(I,A))| = |Hom(I,A)|! since automorphisms permute states. Ax1 guarantees |Hom(I,A)| is finite. Therefore |Aut(A)| is always finite.
V9_finite_automorphisms.consequence: The Lorentz group SO(3,1) is a continuous Lie group (uncountably infinite). It cannot be Aut(A) for any single object A in a finite CCA. This is CCA-IMP-2.

V10_entropy.proof: H(ε) is a deterministic function of ε by definition — no further axiom needed.
V10_entropy.caveat: Different CCAs with different ε have different H values. H is an invariant of a specific CCA, not a universal constant.

V11_transport_non_unique.conclusion: The same CCA (same ε, same causal order) is compatible with horizontal, vertical, and diagonal net current directions. The transport direction is NOT uniquely fixed by Ax1-Ax5. Selecting one direction requires an additional axiom (projection direction, or an explicit direction decomposition e_b). This is the J non-uniqueness result in >1D, proved more cleanly here at the categorical level.

classical_probability.note: Always >= 0; cannot be less than max(p_A, p_B)

V12_no_interference.proof: For real ε ∈ [0,1]: any combination of paths has probability Σ ε(m) ≥ 0. Destructive interference requires a term 2 Re(ψ₁ψ₂*) < 0, impossible for real non-negative amplitudes. Therefore interference is IMPOSSIBLE from Ax1-Ax5 with real ε.
V12_no_interference.conclusion: Target 19: Result (D) — Cannot emerge from Ax1-Ax5.

V13_gap7_structure.conclusion: Models with different v but same λ give IDENTICAL temporal PSD. Only a SPATIAL measurement (ξ_c = v/λ) can distinguish them. This is the structural proof of GAP-7: c is not fixed by temporal observables alone. The P3 ratio c = ξ_c/(2τ_B) requires BOTH spatial AND temporal measurements.

required_conditions.C1_metric_embedding: SE1: phi: O -> R^d (ADDITIONAL AXIOM — not in Ax1-Ax5)
required_conditions.C2_isotropy: Equal step length a in all directions (ADDITIONAL AXIOM)
required_conditions.C3_uniform_time: Equal time step dt per morphism (ADDITIONAL AXIOM)
required_conditions.C4_single_speed: No multiple branches (ADDITIONAL AXIOM or reduction to 1D)

V14_conditional_uniqueness.theorem_statement: CONDITIONAL UNIQUENESS THEOREM: If a CCA satisfies Ax1-Ax5 AND is equipped with: (C1) a metric embedding phi: O -> R^d, (C2) uniform spatial step length a in all directions, (C3) uniform temporal step dt, (C4) a single propagation branch, THEN the propagation speed c = a/dt is uniquely determined. NONE of C1-C4 follows from Ax1-Ax5. Each is an additional axiom.
V14_conditional_uniqueness.conclusion: Speed uniqueness is a conditional theorem: it holds under C1-C4, all of which are external to Ax1-Ax5. The theorem is non-trivial because it identifies the MINIMAL set of additional axioms needed.
